note: From OpenStreetMap's main API (14 October 2026; tools/osm-to-kit.mjs and the export's railway=rail ways), the view from above (docs/reference/aerial/bramhall.jpg) and the photos (docs/reference/photos/bramhall: railbridge-1.jpg Kevin Waterhouse 2024, entrance-1.jpg Peter Barr 2012, shelter-1.jpg JThomas 2024, platform-1.jpg Bill Boaden 2022, platform-2.jpg Nigel Thompson 2013, shelter-2.jpg Graham Hogg 2012, carpark-1.jpg N Chadwick 2014), at real scale: two side platforms of about 173 m on the Macclesfield line, on an embankment, 1.68 m outside its two tracks; platform 1 (the halt's, towards Manchester) on the west side, -v. Positive v is north-east. OpenStreetMap's tracks and platforms lie about 3.7 m further towards -v than the network's tracks do here, so everything from the export is moved 3.7 m towards +v to stand on them. Trains stop 18 m south of the station's point, in the middle of the real platforms, which take six cars as they are; the extension at the south end is the game's. The line crosses Bramhall Lane South on a green girder bridge (MCH/8) just beyond the platforms' north end, drawn square to the line; steps from each platform's north end go down to the road, which is the way across (no footbridge in the export or the photos). The booking office is the small brick building on platform 1 in the export and platform-2.jpg, its roof drawn hipped; the platform narrows in front of it. Glass shelters, cycle racks and the white panelled fence behind the platforms from the photos. The pay-and-display car park west of the line behind platform 1's south half from the export and carpark-1.jpg. The rail replacement buses use Stop B on Bramhall Lane South (the export). Lamps, boards and shelters placed by eye; the canopies, lifts, barriers, kiosk and coffee cart are the game's.
